question: What is the main reason a nurse performs a follow-up check after giving medication?

options.A: To ask the patient to sign the hospital billing forms
options.B: To evaluate if the drug is working and watch for side effects
options.C: To remind the doctor when the next shift starts
options.D: To clean up the leftover water cups from the bedside table

explanation: Follow-up monitoring ensures therapeutic effectiveness and catches early signs of adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h7)

question: Why do our hands and face get a much larger area on the sensory homunculus than our back or thighs?

options.A: They are closer physically to the brain
options.B: They contain larger bones and thicker muscles
options.C: They receive more blood flow from the carotid arteries
options.D: They have a much higher density of sensory receptors

explanation: Spot on! Areas of the body we use for fine, detailed feeling (like fingertips and lips) have way more receptors, so the brain gives them extra processing space.

question: What is the most important home safety change to make in the bathroom after an amputation?

options.A: Replacing all porcelain fixtures with plastic ones
options.B: Removing the bathroom door to improve airflow
options.C: Installing grab bars near the toilet and shower
options.D: Painting the bathroom walls a bright, cheerful color

explanation: Wet bathroom floors plus new mobility challenges spell danger. Grab bars and shower seats keep baths safe and independent!

question: What is the primary purpose of giving a patient a diuretic?

options.A: To increase urine output and remove excess body fluid
options.B: To dissolve hard kidney stones blocking the ureter
options.C: To raise the blood pressure during episodes of fainting
options.D: To stop painful muscle cramps in the lower extremities

explanation: Diuretics make the kidneys flush out extra water and salt, which is wonderful for reducing swelling and fluid overload in conditions like heart failure.

question: What is the main goal of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Building specialized tertiary hospitals in every local government
options.B: Bringing essential health care close to where people live
options.C: Training foreign medical doctors for rural service postings
options.D: Providing free medications for chronic non-communicable diseases

explanation: Spot on! PHC is all about bringing basic, necessary health services right to people's doorsteps or communities, so nobody has to travel miles just to see a nurse or doctor.

question: Which major blood vessel feeds oxygen-rich blood to the small intestine and the first part of the large intestine?

options.A: Superior mesenteric artery
options.B: Celiac trunk
options.C: Inferior mesenteric artery
options.D: Renal artery

explanation: The superior mesenteric artery is the main lifeline branching off the aorta to supply the small intestine and upper colon. Keep crushing it!

question: Why is a quiet, private environment essential when a nurse conducts a telehealth video call?

options.A: To make the nurse's computer battery last much longer during the shift
options.B: To stop other staff members from asking questions about their work
options.C: To ensure compliance with patient privacy and confidentiality laws
options.D: To prevent background noise from interrupting the internet signal

explanation: Conducting calls in private spaces stops unauthorized people from overhearing sensitive health discussions, protecting patient confidentiality. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why should every task on a project checklist be assigned to a specific person?

options.A: To make it easier to fire workers who make minor mistakes
options.B: To ensure only the facility director does any actual work
options.C: To ensure accountability so responsibilities are never neglected
options.D: To prevent team members from communicating with each other

explanation: When everyone is responsible, no one is responsible! Assigning names ensures every important task actually gets done.

question: A nurse notices that outsourced lab staff keep missing deadlines, which delays patient medications. What is the best step for the nurse?

options.A: Perform all laboratory tests independently in addition to standard nursing duties
options.B: Ignore the delays because outsourced staff are outside the nursing department's control
options.C: Advise patients to purchase private insurance to get faster lab results
options.D: Document the delays and report them through proper administrative channels for contract review

explanation: As a patient advocate, document the facts clearly and report them up the administrative chain so management can fix the vendor issue.

question: What does it mean if a research questionnaire is described as 'reliable'?

options.A: It successfully measures complex human emotions accurately
options.B: It has been approved by the hospital ethics committee
options.C: It gives consistent results when used repeatedly over time
options.D: It is completely free from any potential ethical violations

explanation: Reliability is all about consistency. A reliable tool yields similar scores when conditions remain stable. Keep up the great work!

question: What is the primary risk associated with taking potassium-sparing diuretics?

options.A: Hypocalcemia
options.B: Hyperkalemia
options.C: Hyponatremia
options.D: Hypokalemia

explanation: Because these drugs prevent potassium excretion, they can cause potassium levels in the blood to climb too high. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h5)

question: Why is information science an essential pillar for nursing informatics?

options.A: It provides the ethical guidelines for bedside patient care.
options.B: It builds the physical computer towers used at the nurses' station.
options.C: It manufactures the electronic blood pressure cuffs.
options.D: It structures and organizes how clinical data is gathered and analyzed.

explanation: Information science specifically governs how data is organized, structured, and processed to make it meaningful for healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is a great example of secondary data in a community assessment?

options.A: Focus group discussions with local market women
options.B: Direct visual observations of village water sources
options.C: Interviews conducted by nurses during home visits
options.D: Clinic registers and existing census reports

explanation: Spot on! Secondary data is information that was already collected by someone else and is sitting in existing records and reports.

question: Why are vasodilators frequently used in managing severe heart complications?

options.A: They widen blood vessels to reduce the resistance the heart must fight against
options.B: They make the heart beat at maximum speed instantly
options.C: They thicken the blood to raise blood pressure
options.D: They make blood clot much faster

explanation: Imagine trying to push water through a pinched garden hose vs. a wide-open pipe. Vasodilators open up the blood vessels, making it much easier for a tired heart to push blood forward!

question: What is the main goal of managing money in healthcare?

options.A: Transferring financial tasks entirely to the accounting team
options.B: Maximizing profits through reduced patient admissions
options.C: Balancing good patient care with financial responsibility
options.D: Eliminating all operational costs in every department

explanation: You've got this! Financial management is simply about making sure patients get top-notch care while keeping the hospital financially healthy.

question: What is a common medication-related cause of falls in older adults?

options.A: Mild skin irritation from ointments
options.B: Dry mouth from antibiotic use
options.C: Dizziness from blood pressure drugs
options.D: Increased appetite from vitamins

explanation: Medications that lower blood pressure can cause sudden dizziness when a person stands up, leading to a fall. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h3)

question: What important safety rule must nurses follow when discussing research on social media?

options.A: They must ensure their posts are at least ten pages long
options.B: They must strictly protect patient privacy and confidentiality at all times
options.C: They must use only Latin medical terms in their messages
options.D: They are required to pay a tax on every scientific post they share

explanation: Online sharing carries risks of breaching privacy, so nurses must never reveal identifying patient details. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h7)

question: What does a pulse oximeter measure in a patient?

options.A: Blood oxygen saturation levels
options.B: Electrical activity of the heart
options.C: Arterial blood pressure
options.D: Internal core body temperature

explanation: A pulse oximeter shines light through the skin to calculate how much oxygen is carried by the red blood cells. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the common medical term for what we usually call food poisoning?

options.A: Bowel obstruction
options.B: Systemic sepsis
options.C: Foodborne illness
options.D: Gastric influenza

explanation: Foodborne illness is the standard clinical term for sickness caused by eating contaminated food or drink. Great job getting started!

question: Out of these options, which patient situation should a critical care nurse tackle FIRST?

options.A: Dry lips from breathing through an oxygen mask
options.B: Sudden drop in blood pressure with cold, pale skin
options.C: Mild anxiety about upcoming laboratory tests
options.D: Boredom due to lack of television entertainment

explanation: Circulation crashing takes top priority every single time! We can fix dry lips or boredom later, but low BP means the body isn't getting perfused right now.

question: What important instruction should a nurse give a patient who has received dilating eye drops?

options.A: Wear heavy winter gloves to avoid rubbing the eyelids
options.B: Avoid driving because their vision will be temporarily blurred
options.C: Keep their eyes tightly closed for the rest of the day
options.D: Wash their eyes thoroughly with tap water every ten minutes

explanation: Dilating drops paralyze the focusing muscles and dilate the pupil, causing blurry vision and glare, making driving unsafe. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h5)

question: How many escape routes should a good fire safety plan provide for each room?

options.A: As many as there are windows
options.B: Only one main front door
options.C: At least two ways out
options.D: One exit per floor level

explanation: Always plan for two ways out! If fire or thick smoke blocks the main doorway, you need a backup route like a window.

question: What is a standard admission rule for most half-way houses?

options.A: Requirement to work at least forty hours per week immediately
options.B: Promise never to communicate with family members again
options.C: Ability to pay for private medical insurance out of pocket
options.D: Willingness to follow house rules and remain substance-free

explanation: That's correct! To keep the living space safe and healing for everyone, residents agree to stay off illicit substances and respect the facility rules.

question: Why is interactive training better than just handing out printed rulebooks to food handlers?

options.A: It guarantees that workers will pass a written government exam
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future workplace supervision
options.C: It helps workers understand the practical reasons behind safety habits
options.D: It ensures that workers spend less time working in the kitchen

explanation: Demonstrations connect dry rules to real-life risks, making it much easier for staff to actually change their habits. Awesome!

question: Why is writing 'patient seems uncooperative' discouraged in nursing notes?

options.A: It takes too much time to write out compared to numbers
options.B: It prevents doctors from prescribing pain medication
options.C: It is subjective and reflects personal bias rather than facts
options.D: It violates hospital billing guidelines and insurance rules

explanation: Labels like 'uncooperative' are just opinions. Instead, write the clear facts of what happened, like 'patient refused morning vital signs.'

question: What is the main job of sensory receptors in the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: To turn things like touch, heat, and pressure into electrical signals
options.B: To protect delicate nerve bundles from getting crushed
options.C: To release hormones that control your blood pressure
options.D: To tell your skeletal muscles to squeeze tightly

explanation: You nailed it! Sensory receptors act like translators, converting physical feelings from the environment into the electrical language your nerves understand.

question: A patient is admitted after a long period of severe vomiting. Which acid-base imbalance are they most at risk for?

options.A: Metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic acidosis
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Stomach fluid is packed with hydrochloric acid. When a patient vomits it all away, they lose acid and retain excess bicarbonate, leading to metabolic alkalosis.

question: Why must quality assurance decisions be data-driven rather than based on guesswork?

options.A: Data collection completely eliminates all human error
options.B: Data provides accurate proof of where problems exist and if changes actually work
options.C: Hospital management only accepts reports written in numbers
options.D: Guesswork is illegal for registered nurses in Nigeria

explanation: In nursing, we rely on facts! Real data gives us clear proof of what's going wrong and whether our new ideas are actually fixing the problem.

question: Why does long-term poverty often contribute to higher rates of mental health issues?

options.A: Financial worries completely eliminate the need for sleep
options.B: Wealthy people are immune to all forms of emotional distress
options.C: Poor people choose to have weaker brain chemistry
options.D: It exposes individuals to continuous, inescapable daily stress and insecurity

explanation: When someone is constantly struggling to survive and pay bills day after day, their brain's coping reserves get completely worn down.

question: Which of these organs is found in the upper belly (abdominal) part of the abdominopelvic cavity?

options.A: Brain
options.B: Spinal cord
options.C: Urinary bladder
options.D: Stomach

explanation: Your stomach hangs out in the upper tummy area, while your bladder is tucked way down in the pelvis.

question: What happens when a tertiary hospital lacks funds to maintain its intensive care unit?

options.A: The hospital starts generating extra revenue from parking fees
options.B: Patients recover faster by relying on natural rest
options.C: Doctors spend more time teaching medical students
options.D: Critically ill patients experience higher mortality due to broken life support systems

explanation: If ICU equipment and oxygen supplies fail from lack of maintenance, vulnerable patients lose their lives. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is poor staff training during a new technology rollout so dangerous?

options.A: It forces the hospital to close its emergency department
options.B: It makes patients lose trust in the hospital cleaning staff
options.C: It causes hospital computers to catch computer viruses
options.D: It leads to confusion, frustration, and dangerous workarounds

explanation: Exactly! If nurses aren't properly trained on new equipment, stress takes over under pressure, leading to risky shortcuts.

question: What does healthcare outsourcing actually mean?

options.A: Hiring external vendors to perform specific hospital operations or services
options.B: Closing down public health clinics to build private pharmacies
options.C: Permanently selling public hospitals to private business owners
options.D: Transferring clinical nurses to foreign healthcare institutions

explanation: Outsourcing is like hiring an outside expert to handle specific tasks (like security or laundry) while the hospital stays in charge of the big picture.

question: What is the main goal of a sheltered workshop for clients?

options.A: Providing permanent long-term housing
options.B: Maximizing company profit margins
options.C: Replacing traditional hospital care entirely
options.D: Rehabilitation and skill building

explanation: Sheltered workshops are designed to help clients recover and learn useful skills in a safe, supportive space rather than focusing on business profits. You've got this!

question: Why must sexual partners be treated at the same time for a sexually transmitted infection?

options.A: To eliminate the need for follow-up blood tests altogether
options.B: To prevent passing the infection back and forth between partners
options.C: To speed up the manufacturing process of the antibiotic drugs
options.D: To ensure the laboratory costs remain low for the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Treating both partners simultaneously stops the ping-pong effect of reinfecting each other. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h4)

question: Why is gentle hand expression of milk recommended before feeding when a mother's breasts are very swollen (engorged)?

options.A: It softens the areola so the infant can achieve a proper latch
options.B: It replaces the need for any future breastfeeding sessions
options.C: It cures underlying bacterial infections instantly
options.D: It permanently stops milk production in the affected breast

explanation: Severe swelling pulls the nipple flat, making it tricky for the baby to grip. Expressing a little milk first creates a softer surface to grasp. Well done!

question: What does "role ambiguity" mean for a nursing team on the ward?

options.A: Staff members refuse to speak to each other during shifts
options.B: There are not enough wheelchairs available for patients
options.C: The hospital building has confusing hallways and signs
options.D: Nurses are unclear about their exact duties and responsibilities

explanation: Role ambiguity happens when job boundaries are fuzzy. When nobody is quite sure who is supposed to handle a specific task, confusion and frustration naturally follow.

question: A community health nurse wants to help a low-income mother boost her child's protein intake affordably. Which local combination works best?

options.A: Beans and corn or rice
options.B: Imported tinned foreign chocolates
options.C: Pure refined table sugar and water
options.D: Bottled carbonated soft drinks

explanation: Pairing beans with grains like corn or rice is a classic, budget-friendly way to serve complete protein that supports healthy childhood growth.

question: Why is it a drawback to keep a successful quality project locked inside just one nursing unit?

options.A: It prevents other patients and staff from benefiting from proven safer practices
options.B: It causes the original unit to lose funding for their nursing supplies
options.C: It automatically violates hospital licensing and accreditation standards
options.D: It forces the hospital to hire extra consultants from outside the country

explanation: Sharing is caring in nursing! When we keep great improvements hidden in one ward, other patients miss out on safer care.

question: What is an important action to take if a patient tests negative while still within a recent window period?

options.A: Inform the client's employer about their negative status
options.B: Prescribe antiretroviral therapy for lifelong daily use
options.C: Assume the client is fully immune to future HIV exposure
options.D: Schedule a follow-up test after the window period closes

explanation: You got it! Because recent exposure might not show up yet, they need a repeat test later to be 100% sure of their status.

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized factor that influences a patient's ability to adapt to an illness?

options.A: Past life experiences and trauma
options.B: The hospital's interior wall color
options.C: Cultural beliefs regarding health
options.D: Available social and family support

explanation: Internal and external factors like culture, support systems, and personal history deeply affect adaptation, whereas minor environmental aesthetics do not dictate coping capacity. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h4)

question: What does intersectoral collaboration mean in the context of primary health care?

options.A: Nurses working across different shifts in the same hospital ward
options.B: International organizations taking over national health budgets
options.C: Different sectors like agriculture and education working together with health
options.D: Private hospitals competing with government clinics for patients

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration means various non-health sectors partner with health providers to address the wider causes of disease. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of these conditions makes taking a bladder anticholinergic unsafe?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Lower back pain
options.C: Mild hypertension
options.D: Urinary retention

explanation: If a patient already cannot empty their bladder, giving a drug that relaxes the bladder even more will make retention much worse.

question: Why are patients usually advised to take their daily diuretic dose in the morning?

options.A: To match the natural peak of the human hormone cycle
options.B: To stop the drug from interacting with breakfast foods
options.C: To prevent frequent nighttime trips to the toilet that can cause falls
options.D: To ensure maximum absorption while the stomach is completely empty

explanation: Taking diuretics early means the heavy urination happens during the day, letting the patient sleep peacefully at night without risking a fall in the dark!

question: Which class of diuretics is known for being the most powerful at removing fluid from the body?

options.A: Potassium-sparing diuretics
options.B: Loop diuretics
options.C: Thiazide diuretics
options.D: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors

explanation: Loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, where a massive amount of sodium is normally reabsorbed, making them very potent. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of psychological first aid (PFA) when used by nurses in an IDP camp?

options.A: To prescribe strong sedative medications for insomnia
options.B: To cure long-standing clinical schizophrenia permanently
options.C: To diagnose underlying personality disorders in adults
options.D: To offer humane, supportive comfort and reduce immediate distress

explanation: PFA is about listening, offering practical care, and comforting people without forcing them to relive traumatic events.

question: When is the best time to use a multiple line graph?

options.A: When displaying the exact percentages of a single pie chart
options.B: When comparing two or more related trends on the same set of axes
options.C: When listing text instructions for wound dressing changes
options.D: When only a single measurement is taken once in a lifetime

explanation: Correct! When you want to see how two or more groups stack up against each other over the same period, put them on one graph.

question: What proportion of waste produced in health care settings is generally non-hazardous household-like waste?

options.A: 10 to 25 percent
options.B: 95 to 99 percent
options.C: 75 to 90 percent
options.D: 50 to 60 percent

explanation: The vast majority of hospital trash is ordinary non-hazardous waste, just like normal household rubbish. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: Why can't you rely solely on looking at a vaccine to know if heat has ruined it?

options.A: Heat damage does not change the physical appearance of the liquid
options.B: Vaccines change color only when exposed to freezing temperatures
options.C: Expired vaccines always look completely normal to the naked eye
options.D: Modern glass vials are coated with special heat-reflective paint

explanation: Most heat-damaged vaccines look totally normal! That's why temperature logs and Vaccine Vial Monitors (VVMs) are our best friends.

question: When do you need to add Transmission-Based Precautions?

options.A: When a specific infection is known or suspected
options.B: When the nurse starts a new morning shift
options.C: When standard handwashing fails to work
options.D: When the patient requests a private room

explanation: You add these special precautions (like gowns or masks) on top of standard ones whenever you're dealing with a specific germ.

question: Why is patient stability so important when deciding whether or not to delegate a task?

options.A: Stable patients do not require any monitoring from healthcare workers
options.B: Unstable patients always pay more for hospital accommodation
options.C: Stable patients are harder to communicate with than unstable ones
options.D: Unstable patients require continuous clinical judgment that only a registered nurse can provide

explanation: When a patient's condition can change rapidly, it needs a professional nurse's close assessment rather than auxiliary care.

question: Which of these best describes for-profit healthcare providers?

options.A: They are strictly owned and managed by local government councils
options.B: They operate as commercial businesses aiming to generate financial returns
options.C: They offer free medical services to every member of the public
options.D: They rely exclusively on volunteer staff and donated medical supplies

explanation: Correct! For-profit clinics run like businesses, meaning making a financial return is part of keeping their doors open.

question: Which of the following is a major objective of the Mother-Baby Package?

options.A: To reduce maternal, fetal, and newborn mortality rates
options.B: To increase the cost of maternity drugs in local clinics
options.C: To eliminate all traditional birth attendants completely
options.D: To transfer all pregnant women to tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Exactly right! Every clinical guideline and care package ultimately aims to keep both mum and baby safe, healthy, and alive.

question: Why would a healthcare planner choose a Cost-Utility Analysis over a regular Cost-Effectiveness Analysis?

options.A: To calculate only the direct financial profits of a new pharmacy wing
options.B: To evaluate treatments that impact both length of life and patient well-being
options.C: To prove that all medical interventions cost the exact same amount
options.D: To avoid measuring clinical outcomes entirely in hospital settings

explanation: When patient comfort and quality of life matter just as much as living longer, a Cost-Utility Analysis (using QALYs) is the best choice.

question: Which of the following is a primary prevention activity carried out by community nurses against endemic vector-borne diseases?

options.A: Administering intravenous fluids to patients in intensive care units
options.B: Performing complex surgery to remove parasitic worms from the eyes
options.C: Writing prescriptions for strong antibiotics to treat chronic bacterial infections
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated bed nets to pregnant women and children

explanation: Providing bed nets stops mosquito bites before infection can occur, making it a key primary prevention strategy. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h6)

question: How does dietary counselling differ from Medical Nutrition Therapy?

options.A: There is no real difference between the two terms in clinical practice
options.B: Counselling is only done by surgeons in the operating theatre
options.C: MNT is used exclusively for people who want to lose weight for fashion
options.D: Counselling focuses on general healthy eating, whereas MNT treats complex disease states

explanation: Dietary counselling covers general wellness and basic lifestyle tips, while MNT is an intensive clinical treatment for specific diseases. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h5)

question: What connects the tips of the tiny hair-like strands (stereocilia) together in the inner ear?

options.A: Otolith strands
options.B: Tip links
options.C: Calcium bridges
options.D: Kinetic fibers

explanation: Tip links act like tiny microscopic springs that pull open ion channels when the hairs bend. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h5)

question: A patient with frequent malaria infections lives in a neighborhood with stagnant drainage water and poor housing. Which factor is most directly influencing this patient's health?

options.A: A lack of personal interest in health education
options.B: An unavoidable genetic predisposition to mosquito bites
options.C: Environmental and social determinants of health
options.D: An acute psychological response to stress

explanation: Poor living conditions and stagnant water are environmental factors that directly increase exposure to illness. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why are elderly individuals at higher risk for severe burn injuries from hot water?

options.A: Their skin is thinner and loses sensitivity
options.B: They prefer much hotter bath temperatures
options.C: Their homes lack modern plumbing systems
options.D: They spend more time cooking than younger adults

explanation: Thinning skin and reduced nerve sensitivity mean older adults may not feel extreme heat quickly enough to pull away. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why might a misguided healthcare worker agree to perform FGM?

options.A: They are legally required to obey local cultural traditions
options.B: They want to prevent the girl from going to a traditional cutter
options.C: Standard nursing school curricula train them for the procedure
options.D: Hospital management mandates the procedure to generate revenue

explanation: Some clinicians wrongly think they are 'harm reductionists' by doing a 'cleaner cut' than traditional practitioners, but performing FGM is never okay.

question: Why do the bulbourethral glands release a clear mucus right before ejaculation?

options.A: To neutralize any leftover acid from urine in the urethra
options.B: To provide the main energy source for sperm motility
options.C: To activate sperm flagella for faster swimming
options.D: To cause the semen to clot firmly inside the vagina

explanation: Urine is quite acidic and can harm delicate sperm. This clever little mucus fluid cleanses the urethra path first so the sperm can pass safely!

question: Why is hypertension frequently called the 'silent killer'?

options.A: It usually causes no symptoms in its early stages
options.B: Patients refuse to talk about their diagnosis
options.C: It stops the heart without any warning sounds
options.D: It only affects people who are sleeping

explanation: Because high blood pressure rarely causes physical discomfort initially, individuals often remain unaware of their condition until complications arise. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h3)

question: Why are nursing audits so important for quality assurance?

options.A: They reduce the cost of purchasing hospital medications
options.B: They help discover gaps between standard care and actual practice
options.C: They guarantee that patients will never experience complications
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for physician supervision

explanation: Spot on! By comparing what we actually do against established guidelines, audits show us clearly where our care needs a little extra boost.

question: About how much does a normal pregnant woman's total blood volume increase?

options.A: 5 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 10 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Amazing right? The body ramps up blood volume by about half to care for both the mother and the growing baby. That's why iron and fluids are so crucial!

question: How does a just culture handle a nurse who makes an honest, unintentional mistake?

options.A: By reporting them to the police for criminal negligence
options.B: By immediately terminating their employment without a formal hearing
options.C: By ignoring the incident entirely to protect team morale
options.D: By offering coaching, support, and looking at the system flaws that contributed

explanation: Honest mistakes are treated as learning opportunities involving system factors, rather than automatic grounds for harsh discipline. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h2)

question: Why do we often see long waiting lists in healthcare instead of a quick market balance?

options.A: Prices are often distorted or subsidized, causing demand to outstrip supply
options.B: Doctors refuse to treat patients until their medical conditions worsen
options.C: Patients prefer waiting months for elective procedures to save money
options.D: Hospitals deliberately hide available beds to inflate treatment costs

explanation: You nailed it. When care is heavily subsidized or cheap, everyone rushes in, and soon there are more patients than available beds or staff.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core elements of Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: Contraceptive and family planning services
options.B: Treatment of abortion-related medical complications
options.C: Counseling for emotional and reproductive needs
options.D: Routine major abdominal surgery for all patients

explanation: Spot on! Routine major surgery is not part of PAC. Complications are usually managed with minor procedures like MVA or medical treatment.

question: What is the main goal of psychiatric rehabilitation?

options.A: To keep patients in hospital care permanently
options.B: To isolate patients from their families forever
options.C: To cure mental illness using only herbal remedies
options.D: To help patients return to meaningful community life

explanation: You got this! Psychiatric rehabilitation is all about helping individuals with long-term mental health challenges regain their independence and live fulfilling lives back in society.

question: How does the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) protect the public from unsafe practice?

options.A: By setting scopes of practice, licensing nurses, and enforcing discipline
options.B: By providing free housing for newly graduated nurses
options.C: By hiring domestic staff for community health centers
options.D: By managing the financial budgets of all private hospitals

explanation: Spot on! By licensing only qualified practitioners and keeping an eye on professional conduct, the NMCN ensures patients are always in safe hands.

question: How can you tell if a patient has a typical post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It only hurts when the patient eats or drinks
options.B: It disappears completely when the room is dark
options.C: It gets worse when the patient sits or stands up
options.D: It stays the exact same intensity all day long

explanation: You nailed it! These headaches get worse when upright because of lower fluid pressure around the brain, and they feel better when lying flat.

question: A shortage of which mineral leads to an enlarged thyroid gland, known as a goiter?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Iron
options.D: Zinc

explanation: You got it! Iodine helps the thyroid gland make important hormones. Without enough iodine, the thyroid swells up, causing a goiter. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe home modification for preventing mobility-related falls?

options.A: Ensuring bright and steady lighting along hallway floors
options.B: Placing loose decorative throw rugs over slippery tile floors
options.C: Installing grab bars securely next to the toilet and shower
options.D: Clearing electrical cords completely out of walking pathways

explanation: Loose throw rugs slide easily under feet or assistive devices, making them a major hazard for causing patient falls. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h6)

question: What is the name of the temperature range known as the 'Danger Zone' where bacteria multiply super fast?

options.A: 0°C to 10°C
options.B: 5°C to 60°C
options.C: Minus 10°C to 0°C

explanation: Remember: 5°C to 60°C is the sweet spot for bacteria to throw a party and multiply rapidly. Keep hot foods hot and cold foods cold!

question: If a research study is 'verifiable,' what does that mean for other nurses?

options.A: The study can only be performed once in history
options.B: Only the original author is allowed to read the data
options.C: Other researchers can replicate it and get similar results
options.D: The results change every time a new nurse looks at them

explanation: You got it! Verifiable means another nurse or researcher can repeat your steps and find the same results, proving it's trustworthy.

question: How do internal audits differ from external audits?

options.A: Internal audits are voluntary suggestions, while external audits are completely illegal
options.B: Internal audits happen once every decade, while external audits happen every morning
options.C: Internal audits are done within the facility, while external ones are done by independent outside bodies
options.D: Internal audits focus only on doctors, while external audits focus only on nurses

explanation: You got it! Internal checks are done by your own hospital team to catch mistakes early, while external checks are done by independent outsiders for an unbiased review.

question: Why does a repeat infection with the same virus trigger a much faster immune response?

options.A: Memory B-cells formed during the first infection quickly recognize the virus.
options.B: Red blood cells absorb the viral toxins before they reach the lymph nodes.
options.C: Innate white blood cells stop destroying friendly bacteria in the gut.
options.D: The body's skin barriers become thicker to prevent the virus from entering.

explanation: Memory B-cells remember past battles, letting your body skip the slow setup phase and fight back instantly.

question: What key stage of a parasite's life cycle happens inside its definitive host?

options.A: The parasite reaches maturity and reproduces sexually
options.B: The parasite dies off because the immune system is too strong
options.C: The parasite transforms directly into an ectoparasite
options.D: The parasite only undergoes brief larval resting stages

explanation: You're doing great! The definitive host is the VIP lounge for the parasite—it's where they finally grow up into adults and reproduce.

question: What makes a Type B drug reaction so tricky compared to other reactions?

options.A: It can always be calculated using the patient's exact weight
options.B: It disappears completely if the patient drinks more water
options.C: It happens suddenly and does not depend on the dose
options.D: It only occurs when the drug expires on the shelf

explanation: Type B reactions are bizarre and unexpected. They can happen out of nowhere, no matter if the dose is tiny or large!

question: How do vaccines protect the human body against specific diseases?

options.A: Destroying all bacteria currently living in the gut
options.B: Increasing the overall body temperature to kill viruses
options.C: Stimulating antibody production without causing illness
options.D: Providing permanent chemical antibiotics in the blood

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines introduce harmless pieces or weakened parts of a germ so your immune system can safely learn to fight it without getting you sick.

question: A farmer arrives at the clinic drooling, tearing up, peeing frequently, and having muscle twitches after spraying the farm. What is this?

options.A: Sedative overdose from sleeping pills
options.B: Cholinergic poisoning from organophosphates
options.C: Caustic poisoning from swallowed acid
options.D: Opioid poisoning from strong painkillers

explanation: Correct! Remember the DUMBELS sign (drooling, urination, muscle twitching, etc.)—it points straight to organophosphate poisoning.

question: What is a key nursing action to prevent bedsores (pressure injuries) in immobile residents?

options.A: Applying strong antiseptic ointment to all bony areas
options.B: Limiting fluid intake to prevent skin moisture
options.C: Keeping the resident in bed twenty-four hours a day
options.D: Implementing regular repositioning schedules

explanation: Spot on! Turning and repositioning patients regularly takes the weight off bony spots, keeping their skin safe and healthy.

question: What is the best way to get nursing staff on board when introducing a new bedside charting system?

options.A: Keeping all details about the new system secret until the launch day
options.B: Involving frontline nurses in the planning process and providing clear, supportive training
options.C: Forcing staff to use the new system immediately without any prior explanation or training
options.D: Threatening disciplinary action for anyone who asks questions about the new software

explanation: Brilliant! Involving nurses early and training them well makes everyone feel confident and turns resistance into teamwork.

question: Which of these details is NOT needed when documenting a medication you gave to a patient?

options.A: The physiological response observed in the patient
options.B: The personal home address of the dispensing pharmacist
options.C: The precise time and date the drug was given
options.D: The exact dosage and administration route used

explanation: Spot on! The pharmacist's address has nothing to do with patient care. Your chart is all about the drug, the time, and how the patient reacted.

question: Which eye sign is a classic warning sign of advanced Vitamin A deficiency?

options.A: Enlarged goiter
options.B: Conjunctival pallor
options.C: Jaundiced sclera
options.D: Bitot's spots

explanation: You're right! Bitot's spots look like little foamy, dry patches on the white part of the eye, telling us the child badly needs Vitamin A. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of family planning?

options.A: Permanently stopping population growth in rural areas
options.B: Deciding the number and spacing of children
options.C: Ensuring every woman gives birth in a hospital
options.D: Treating all known sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Spot on! Family planning simply helps couples and individuals choose how many kids they want and the best time to have them.

question: Why do doctors request sensitivity testing before starting targeted antibiotic treatment?

options.A: To prove that the patient has never been exposed to the germ before
options.B: To ensure the chosen drug effectively kills the specific infecting strain
options.C: To confirm that the infection is definitely caused by a fungus or virus
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing expensive brand-name drugs

explanation: Sensitivity testing takes out the guesswork, making sure we pick the exact antibiotic that will knock out the patient's specific infection.

question: In community health, how would you classify poor sanitation and crowded living conditions?

options.A: The host
options.B: The environment
options.C: The clinical symptom
options.D: The infectious agent

explanation: Spot on! External surroundings like crowding and sanitation fall directly under the environmental part of the triad.

question: Why is rapid access to patient information critical for nurses at the bedside?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal patient handovers
options.B: It eliminates the need for physical patient assessments
options.C: It allows nurses to diagnose surgical conditions alone
options.D: It prevents treatment delays and duplicate testing

explanation: Having quick access to past medical history and test results helps nurses avoid repeating tests and speeds up safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a 'test of change' in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To conduct a massive clinical trial on new surgical equipment
options.B: To try out a new idea on a small scale before full implementation
options.C: To permanently rewrite the national nursing practice guidelines
options.D: To punish staff who fail to follow standard hospital operating procedures

explanation: A test of change simply means trying out a new workflow or idea on a small scale first. It lets your team experiment safely without turning the whole hospital upside down!

question: How can a tele-nurse make sure a patient truly understood instructions given during a video call?

options.A: Ask the patient to repeat the instructions back in their own words.
options.B: Assume understanding if the patient nods once during the video call.
options.C: Send a written legal contract via email for signature.
options.D: Check the patient's medical history for past compliance.

explanation: This is called the 'teach-back' method, and it's a brilliant way to ensure clear communication without making the patient feel tested.

question: What is a major plus when you use seasonal food ingredients for a menu?

options.A: It guarantees that all meals will be completely fat-free
options.B: It removes all cultural restrictions from the meal plan
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for food preservation
options.D: It lowers food costs and guarantees ingredient freshness

explanation: In-season foods are harvested locally in plenty, making them cheaper and way fresher for the kitchen.

question: How do conceptual frameworks help bedside nurses in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: By helping them understand patient behaviors and treatment responses
options.B: By managing the supply inventory in the treatment room
options.C: By replacing the need to document vital signs in charts
options.D: By calculating the monthly salary of nursing staff

explanation: Frameworks give us a clear lens to understand why our patients react to illnesses and treatments the way they do.

question: Which of these is a great example of a clear, SMART project objective?

options.A: Make the hospital a much safer place for all patients
options.B: Fix all communication problems between doctors and nurses
options.C: Decrease missed medication times by twenty percent over three months
options.D: Improve nursing morale whenever possible during shifts

explanation: You nailed it! This goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound—unlike vague statements that leave you guessing.

question: What is the main cause behind the development of a child's behaviour disorder?

options.A: A single genetic mutation inherited from the father
options.B: A complex mix of biological and environmental factors
options.C: Watching television programs after bedtime
options.D: Poor dietary habits during early childhood

explanation: Think of it as a puzzle: genetics, brain function, and family or social environment all combine to influence these behaviors.

question: Which group of patients is usually most at risk for catching hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Athletes with minor muscular sprains
options.B: Children with mild seasonal allergies
options.C: Healthy young adults visiting friends
options.D: Elderly patients receiving immune-suppressing medications

explanation: Correct! Older age plus medications that lower immunity make these patients much more vulnerable to infections.

question: Why is the time spent bathing a patient so great for building the nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: It forces the patient to follow every single hospital rule without arguing
options.B: It gives the patient a chance to voice hidden fears and ask questions
options.C: It allows the nurse to complete all nursing documentation for the shift
options.D: It proves to the doctor that the nurse can complete physical tasks quickly

explanation: Spot on! That quiet, one-on-one time makes patients feel safe and cared for, often opening up about worries they wouldn't share in a busy hallway.

question: What causes swollen blood vessels (esophageal varices) in advanced liver cirrhosis?

options.A: High pressure in the portal vein forcing blood into smaller collateral vessels
options.B: Direct viral attack on the mucosal lining of the esophagus
options.C: Excessive stomach acid production rising into the upper airway
options.D: Swallowing sharp food particles that scrape the throat

explanation: When the scarred liver blocks blood flow, it causes a traffic jam called portal hypertension. Blood has to find other routes, swelling up fragile veins around the esophagus.

question: Which immediate complication happens when an instrument accidentally punctures the muscular wall of the uterus during a procedure?

options.A: Secondary amenorrhea
options.B: Cervical incompetence
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Uterine perforation

explanation: Uterine perforation occurs when sharp instruments or foreign objects poke a hole right through the wall of the uterus. It's a surgical emergency you'll want to watch out for during recovery!

question: If a patient has a very weak immune system, which type of drug do they urgently need to fight an infection?

options.A: Bactericidal
options.B: Bacteriostatic
options.C: Antihistamine
options.D: Topical antiseptic

explanation: Since their immune system can't finish the job, they need bactericidal drugs to directly kill the bacteria for them.

question: A post-abortion patient suddenly develops severe chest pain and shortness of breath on the ward. What should you do right away?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to report the finding
options.B: Discharging the patient home for rest
options.C: Requesting immediate consultation with the appropriate medical specialist
options.D: Telling the patient that chest pain is normal after an abortion

explanation: Chest pain and trouble breathing are red flags. Unstable symptoms like these mean you need to call for a specialist review right away.

question: You are monitoring a woman in active labor and notice a sudden, dangerous spike in her blood pressure. Which tool helped you catch this?

options.A: Sphygmomanometer
options.B: Umbilical cord clamp
options.C: Surgical needle holder
options.D: Mucus extractor

explanation: The sphygmomanometer and stethoscope are your go-to tools for blood pressure checks, helping you spot risky conditions like pre-eclampsia early.

question: A lecturer leaves an anatomical chart displayed on the board long after the topic has changed to nursing ethics. What mistake has the lecturer made?

options.A: Poor timing and management of visual distraction
options.B: Failing to check the cost of the material
options.C: Using an inaccurate scientific model
options.D: Selecting a non-projected visual aid

explanation: Leaving media displayed after the discussion has moved on distracts learners and dilutes the focus of the current lesson. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h5)

question: What is the purpose of an EMR audit trail?

options.A: To automatically record every time a user opens or views a patient chart
options.B: To measure how fast a patient recovers from surgery
options.C: To monitor how many steps a nurse walks during a 12-hour shift
options.D: To track how much money the hospital spends on computer maintenance

explanation: An audit trail leaves a digital footprint, tracking who looked at a patient's file and exactly when they opened it.

question: What is the main goal of psychiatric-mental health nursing?

options.A: Confining dangerous individuals to secure wards
options.B: Promoting health and caring for mental alterations
options.C: Prescribing long-term psychotropic medications
options.D: Isolating patients from community stressors

explanation: As psychiatric nurses, our heart is in holistic care—helping patients build wellness, easing distress, and supporting them through tough emotional times.

question: Why might a cancer care plan shift from trying to cure the disease to focusing purely on comfort and palliation?

options.A: Standard surgical options are suddenly much safer than outpatient chemotherapy.
options.B: The patient's insurance policy has expired and can no longer cover active medications.
options.C: The nursing staff prefers managing comfort care over administering toxic drugs.
options.D: The disease has progressed beyond the point where a cure or control is realistically achievable.

explanation: Spot on! When the disease advances past where treatment can stop it, the healthcare team shifts gears to palliation—focusing entirely on comfort, symptom relief, and quality of life.

question: A nurse evaluates a disaster program and notices residents still cannot point out their local evacuation route. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Remove all warning signs to encourage independent learning
options.B: Report the community residents to local law enforcement
options.C: Assume the community is fully prepared and stop teaching
options.D: Change up the teaching style and provide follow-up education

explanation: You nailed it! Finding a learning gap just means it's time to try a new teaching approach so the community feels confident and prepared.

question: A patient with stable blood pressure comes to a clinic after losing their home in a disaster, and their blood pressure is suddenly very high. Why?

options.A: An intentional overdose of emergency relief food
options.B: Exposure to cold weather causing elevated heart rates
options.C: Disruption of routine medication access and extreme environmental stress
options.D: Sudden permanent cure of their baseline hypertension

explanation: Spot on! Disasters cut off regular medications and create heavy stress, which easily triggers spikes in conditions like high blood pressure.

question: A community health nurse working in a rural Nigerian primary health care clinic is struggling to store vaccines properly due to frequent power outages. Which underlying systemic issue does this practical challenge highlight?

options.A: The total failure of the community participation principle
options.B: An overabundance of highly trained specialist surgeons in the village
options.C: Infrastructure deficits like erratic electricity affecting basic service delivery
options.D: A lack of willingness from mothers to immunize their babies

explanation: Logistical challenges such as power failures and supply chain gaps remain real hurdles in many Nigerian primary health centers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h4)

question: What do we call the exercise where the nurse moves the patient's joint for them, without the patient doing any work?

options.A: Active-assisted movement
options.B: Passive range-of-motion exercise
options.C: Isometric muscle contraction
options.D: Resistive weight-training exercise

explanation: Correct! 'Passive' means the patient is relaxed while you do the moving to keep their joints nice and flexible.

question: What is the main purpose of a living will?

options.A: To divide a deceased person's financial estate among relatives
options.B: To guarantee that a patient receives aggressive life support
options.C: To outline a person's medical treatment preferences before they lose capacity
options.D: To appoint a lawyer for hospital lawsuits

explanation: A living will lets a person state ahead of time what medical treatments they do or don't want if they become too ill to speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h5)

question: What word describes a factor that increases the strength of a heart contraction?

options.A: Positive dromotrope
options.B: Negative chronotrope
options.C: Negative lusitrope
options.D: Positive inotrope

explanation: 'Ino-' relates to force. So a positive inotrope is a substance or factor that boosts the heart's squeezing power. You'll see this often in pharmacology!

question: What usually happens when healthcare workers communicate poorly after a mistake?

options.A: Patients recover much faster from their physical injuries
options.B: Families feel ignored and are more likely to seek legal action
options.C: The hospital administration praises the staff for protecting privacy
options.D: Insurance companies automatically pay out large claims

explanation: When we act defensively or fail to communicate well, families feel disrespected. Out of frustration, they are much more likely to take legal action.

question: An adverse event is best described as an injury that:

options.A: Results from medical management rather than the illness
options.B: Always results from extreme medical negligence
options.C: Only happens during major surgical procedures
options.D: Stops a patient from ever recovering fully

explanation: Think of an adverse event as any unintended medical injury linked to the care provided, whether it could have been prevented or not.

question: How can you help a patient who complains that their low-sodium food tastes too bland?

options.A: Allow the patient to use regular table salt if they eat half the meal
options.B: Remove the food tray and wait until the next scheduled mealtime
options.C: Suggest using herbs, citrus, and salt-free spice blends for flavor
options.D: Tell the patient that bland food is a mandatory part of healing

explanation: Wonderful! Herbs, garlic, and lemon juice add fantastic flavor without any harmful sodium, making healthy eating much easier.

question: Why are greenstick fractures much more common in young children than in adults?

options.A: Children have much higher calcium levels in their bones.
options.B: Children experience lower impact forces during play.
options.C: Children's bones lack a periosteum protective layer.
options.D: Children's bones are softer and more flexible.

explanation: Kids' bones are still growing, so they tend to bend and splinter on one side like a fresh green twig rather than snapping completely.

question: Why do many survivors of FGM experience chronic sexual dysfunction and pain?

options.A: Infections permanently damage the brain's pleasure centers
options.B: Hormonal imbalances stop the ovaries from functioning
options.C: The uterus shrinks and rejects hormonal signals
options.D: Removal of sensitive nerve endings and severe scar tissue cause physical pain and loss of sensation

explanation: That's correct! Removing the clitoris takes away key nerve endings, and the resulting scar tissue makes intimacy physically painful.

question: What is the simplest way families can kill germs in drinking water at home?

options.A: Filtration
options.B: Boiling
options.C: Freezing
options.D: Sedimentation

explanation: That's right! Bringing water to a rolling boil is a quick, reliable way to kill disease-causing organisms right in your kitchen.

question: How should a nursing team view a test that doesn't show the expected improvement during the Study phase?

options.A: As a valuable learning opportunity to understand what does not work
options.B: As a personal failure of every nurse working on the hospital ward
options.C: As proof that quality improvement projects are completely useless
options.D: As a sign that they should hide the data from the nursing director

explanation: Exactly! In QI, even a failed test teaches us something useful. It brings us one step closer to what actually works.

question: Which of the following is an example of print IEC material?

options.A: Illustrated leaflets and posters
options.B: Radio jingles and community songs
options.C: Traditional dance and town criers
options.D: Live theatrical drama skits

explanation: Print materials rely on visual text and graphics, such as leaflets, flyers, and posters, to convey health messages. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h3)

question: A patient is medically ready to leave the ward, but has no home, money, or family support. Who is best suited to help?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The laboratory scientist
options.C: The medical social worker
options.D: The chief operating surgeon

explanation: Medical social workers are champions at discharge planning! They help find shelter and connect vulnerable patients with community support systems.

question: Why are health and learning considered intertwined in school health philosophy?

options.A: Healthy children achieve better academic outcomes
options.B: Schools get extra funding for running clinics
options.C: Teachers are legally required to give out medications
options.D: Academic tests measure physical fitness levels

explanation: A child must be physically and mentally well to fully engage with and benefit from classroom instruction. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of nutrition counselling in primary health care?

options.A: Guiding food choices to promote health and prevent disease
options.B: Prescribing expensive nutritional supplements for every patient
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital dietary restrictions on communities
options.D: Diagnosing rare metabolic disorders in a laboratory setting

explanation: Nutrition counselling focuses on helping clients make healthy food choices to prevent illness and support overall wellness in primary care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why does cholera spread so fast during heavy rains and floods in crowded areas?

options.A: Mosquito populations multiply rapidly in stagnant pools of water.
options.B: Floodwaters easily contaminate public drinking water sources with sewage.
options.C: Airborne dust carries the cholera bacteria across long distances.
options.D: Cold weather lowers human immune systems against bacterial toxins.

explanation: Cholera is waterborne! When floodwaters mix with sewage, people accidentally drink contaminated water, leading to rapid outbreaks.

question: Why is preventing hypothermia so crucial when treating trauma victims?

options.A: It prevents the need for any intravenous fluids.
options.B: Cold temperatures increase blood pressure to dangerous levels.
options.C: Cold bodies cause blood clotting mechanisms to fail and worsen bleeding.
options.D: Hypothermia makes patients sleep through their injuries.

explanation: Correct! A cold body cannot clot blood properly. Along with acid build-up and clotting failures, cold makes bleeding much harder to control.

question: A patient with mild kidney disease is denied a standard heart medication because the doctor worries about organ damage. What does this show?

options.A: Forgetting to check the patient's medical history chart
options.B: Failing to prescribe due to high pharmacy costs
options.C: Deliberately stopping all medications during palliative care
options.D: Withholding therapy out of fear rather than adjusting the dose

explanation: You've got this! Instead of finding a safe dose adjusted for the kidneys, the doctor avoided the drug entirely out of fear.

question: Why do patients taking oral theophylline need regular blood tests?

options.A: It prevents the development of tolerance to the bronchodilator effect
options.B: Blood tests are the only way to measure how well the airways are widening
options.C: The medication is rapidly destroyed by stomach acid without constant monitoring
options.D: The drug has a narrow safety margin between therapeutic and toxic levels

explanation: Theophylline is tricky: too little does nothing, and too much can cause dangerous side effects. Regular blood checks ensure the dose is right in the safe, helpful zone.

question: Why do certain odors often trigger strong emotional memories?

options.A: Because the olfactory cortex connects directly to the limbic system
options.B: Because smell signals are processed first by the visual association area
options.C: Because taste buds share nerve pathways with the emotional centers
options.D: Because the thalamus amplifies scent signals during sleep

explanation: The limbic system is the emotional and memory center of the brain, and its direct link to smell explains this strong connection. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why is keeping a close eye on a recovering patient's nervous system so important after asphyxia?

options.A: To prevent the development of peripheral edema
options.B: To detect early signs of secondary brain injury
options.C: To calculate the correct maintenance fluid rate
options.D: To measure the exact volume of daily urine output

explanation: Brain tissue hates being starved of oxygen. Even after breathing is restored, nurses monitor neuro status closely to catch any delayed swelling or drops in consciousness right away.

question: What does cost-effective healthcare mean in simple terms?

options.A: Charging patients double the price for basic nursing care
options.B: Achieving the best health outcomes with the fewest resources
options.C: Employing only student nurses to avoid paying salaries
options.D: Refusing to buy any modern drugs or equipment

explanation: You got it! Cost-effectiveness is about getting the best possible health results without wasting hard-earned money or supplies.

question: What is a major sign that a patient is struggling to breathe during an emergency check?

options.A: A calm, relaxed face
options.B: Warm, dry skin with pink nail beds
options.C: A steady pulse of 72 beats per minute
options.D: Working hard to breathe and low oxygen saturation

explanation: You nailed it! When a patient is visibly struggling for breath and their oxygen levels drop, it's a clear warning sign that their breathing needs urgent help.

question: What is a common spark or trigger that sets off an acute episode of illness anxiety?

options.A: Engaging in regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Receiving routine blood pressure checks
options.C: Major life stressor or personal loss
options.D: Consuming too much dietary sodium daily

explanation: When life throws a major stressor or emotional pain our way, dormant health worries can flare up into full clinical anxiety.

question: What are early warning signs of a psychiatric relapse?

options.A: Immediate physical healing of a broken bone
options.B: Winning an award at work or school
options.C: Sudden complete recovery and happiness
options.D: Subtle changes like trouble sleeping, irritability, and withdrawing from others

explanation: Early warning signs are small behavioral or emotional shifts that appear before a major crisis occurs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: Your study proves a new handwashing technique cuts down ward infections. Where should you explain how ward nurses can use this daily?

options.A: In the discussion and nursing implications section
options.B: In the abstract summary at the very beginning
options.C: In the methodology and participant selection chapter
options.D: In the raw data tables of the results section

explanation: This is where research meets the bedside—translating your findings into practical steps for everyday nursing care.

question: Why do doctors and nurses usually put a patient on a fluid diet?

options.A: To give the gastrointestinal tract a rest while providing hydration
options.B: To permanently replace normal chewing and digestive functions
options.C: To supply high levels of dietary fiber for bowel regularity
options.D: To rapidly increase body weight in malnourished individuals

explanation: When the tummy needs a break after illness or surgery, fluid diets provide easy hydration without overworking the gut. You've got this!

question: What can happen if you use the wrong liquid (diluent) to mix a vaccine?

options.A: It can destroy the vaccine or harm the client
options.B: It doubles the number of active doses inside the vial
options.C: It automatically turns the liquid into a bright blue color
options.D: It extends the expiration date by exactly six months

explanation: Every vaccine has a specific liquid made just for it. Using the wrong one ruins the dose and compromises patient safety.

question: What is a common sign of compassion fatigue in disaster nurses?

options.A: Emotional numbness, irritability, and burnout
options.B: Increased energy and enthusiasm for work
options.C: Complete indifference to physical illnesses
options.D: An intense desire to work double shifts daily

explanation: Absorbing too much trauma without adequate recovery leads to emotional exhaustion and classic signs of burnout. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h8)

question: What does a color change on a chemical indicator strip tell you?

options.A: That the autoclave machine needs immediate factory maintenance
options.B: That the instrument set is sterile and safe for immediate surgery
options.C: That every single bacterial spore inside the pack is completely dead
options.D: That the package was exposed to the required physical conditions

explanation: Chemical strips only show that heat or gas reached the outside of the pack. They are a great clue, but not a 100% guarantee of internal sterility!

question: Who should be part of the team planning safety for a big public event?

options.A: Private security guards and catering staff only
options.B: Only the venue owners and local ticket vendors
options.C: Organizers, police, fire services, and healthcare leaders
options.D: Elected politicians and international press agencies

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Keeping a big crowd safe takes everyone—from event planners to healthcare pros and emergency services.

question: Why is writing a detailed clinical history on the lab form so important when sending off a skin biopsy?

options.A: It determines how much money the laboratory will bill the patient's insurance
options.B: It dictates the type of suture material that should be used in the clinic
options.C: It proves to the hospital administration that the procedure was strictly necessary
options.D: It guides the pathologist on what specific features to look for under the microscope
